current.text: Experts expect him to keep his starting spot next to McCollum, Daniels, Johnson and Okongwu. If Lu Dort starts, he would likely replace McCollum, not Alexander-Walker. Kingston Flemings is not expected to start over him.
If Dort starts in place of McCollum, Alexander-Walker should get more shots and assists.
Trae Young is gone from Atlanta, and the Hawks added no one to replace him. Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.
Experts see his role, minutes and time on the ball as unchanged from last season.

His second-half shooting last season (about 70% true shooting, about 95% FT, 46 to 48% from three) will not hold. Experts use his pre All-Star line (about 20 points, 58% true shooting) as the baseline. About 81% FT and about 40% from three would still be fine.
Experts rank him inside the top 50 in category leagues, probably inside the top 40. Lloyd projects him 35th. They say he is going too low in drafts and call him free money.
His points league value matches his ADP. His extra value is in category leagues.
In October mock drafts he went anywhere from the early 40s to the 60s, and 50th in one.
Experts call him good value around pick 49 and in rounds 4 to 5.
In one auction mock he went for 14 USD.
Josh values him as a mid 20s USD auction player.
He may have room for more steals. He turned 36.7% of his deflections into steals, up from 29%, and got more deflections in his bigger offensive role.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not a concern.
Atlanta is projected to win about 46 games and finish fourth to eighth in the East.

durable.text: He has been one of the better catch-and-shoot three-point shooters in the NBA for three seasons.
Before his jump to about 90% last season, he shot 77 to 80% from the line on low volume.
Coach Quin Snyder runs an egalitarian, high-movement offense that wants lots of threes and five-out spacing.

note: He averages 5.7 USD on Yahoo and 11.7 USD on ESPN. His site values are 17 and 22 USD, and Josh puts him in the mid 20s, so he is a clear value target near 15 to 20 USD. Even with his shooting coming down, the projections (3.0 threes, about 88% FT on 3.5 attempts, 19 points, 1.1 steals) carry no weak category, so he fits any build and helps 3PM and FT% most. Early in the season, check that his FT% stays well above his old 77 to 80% level, that he keeps about 32 minutes, and whether Dort ends up starting in place of McCollum, which would give him more shots.
